title: Executive sponsor touchpoint + customer quarterly recap email playbook
body:
Purpose
This file is a compact, practical playbook with copy-ready templates for two high-leverage outcomes: (A) a short executive sponsor touchpoint agenda (for 1:1s with customer execs) and (B) a customer-facing quarterly recap email. It also includes a lightweight renewal-playbook checklist and a sample mini renewal tracker you can paste into a spreadsheet or CRM.

Notes on tone and usage
- Keep exec touchpoints concise: 20–30 minutes maximum. Focus on outcomes, risks, asks.
- The customer-facing recap email should celebrate wins, surface measurable value, and close with a clear next step (review + next meeting or renewal cadence).
- Use account-specific metrics; replace placeholders like {{CUSTOMER_NAME}} and {{SPONSOR_NAME}}.

1) Executive Sponsor Touchpoint — 20 minute agenda (template)
Subject: Quick touchpoint: {{CUSTOMER_NAME}} x Redwood — high level check-in
Participants: Executive sponsor (customer), CSM (owner), Solutions lead (optional)
Duration: 20 min
Agenda (timed):
- 0:00–02:00 — Quick hello and confirm timebox / objective (CSM)
- 02:00–07:00 — Top-line health snapshot: adoption, uptime, major wins (CSM)
    - Key metric bullets: active routes, p95 latency, monthly tokens, error rate, cost per 1k tokens (if customer cares)
- 07:00–13:00 — Business outcomes / customer success stories since last touch (customer wins, product features enabled)
- 13:00–17:00 — Risks & blockers (capacity, integration, security, budget) + mitigation plan (CSM)
- 17:00–19:00 — Ask / decisions needed from exec or procurement (e.g., renewal timeframe, budget commit, pilot expansion)
- 19:00–20:00 — Confirm next steps, owners, and date for follow-up

Prep checklist for CSM (before the call)
- One-pager health snapshot (1 slide / doc) with 3 KPIs and trend lines
- 1 success story sentence + quote (if available)
- Top 2 risks with mitigations and owners
- Renewal posture and ask (if relevant)
- Calendar invite with shared agenda + 48 hour reminder email

Quick script (30–45s opener)
"Thanks for making time — we’ll keep this tight. Two quick things to surface: a short snapshot of how Redwood is performing for you, and one or two decisions where your view is helpful. No longer than 20 minutes."

2) Customer-facing Quarterly Recap Email (copy-ready)
Subject line suggestions:
- "Q{quarter} Recap: {{CUSTOMER_NAME}} + Redwood — Key wins & next steps"
- "{{CUSTOMER_NAME}} — Redwood quarterly recap and suggested next steps"

Email body (formal template):
Hi {{SPONSOR_NAME}} and the {{CUSTOMER_NAME}} leadership team,

Hope you’re well — quick quarterly recap from Redwood to summarize value delivered, items to watch, and our recommended next steps. We’ll keep this short.

1) Top-line outcomes (what changed this quarter)
- Production uptime: {{UPTIME}}
- Average p95 latency on main workload: {{P95_LATENCY}}
- Monthly tokens processed: {{MONTHLY_TOKENS}} (+{{%}} vs prior quarter)
- Feature usage: {{FEATURE}} enabled X teams; reduced manual work by Y hours (estimate)

2) Customer wins / case examples (one or two bullets)
- [Example] Support routing automation saved the operations team ~40 hrs/month; accuracy improved from 72% to 88%.
- [Example] Embedded assistant handled 25% of self-serve queries, deflecting ~300 tickets/month.

3) Ops & health (signals we’re watching)
- Error rate / incident highlights: {{ERROR_RATE}}; recent incidents resolved in mean time {{MTTR}}
- Capacity / scaling: average GPU saturation {{GPU_SAT}}; forecast for next quarter suggests {{NEED_ADD}} if growth > {{THRESHOLD}}

4) Product / roadmap alignment (what we plan to deliver that matters to you)
- Short bullets of features or infra changes (e.g., quantization profile, caching improvements, new embedding index support) and expected delivery window

5) Ask / Decisions (clear CTA)
- Recommend a 30-minute review meeting to align on renewal window and any capacity needs. Proposed week of: {{WEEK}}
- If renewal decision is required this quarter: proposed commercial options (1) renew current committed capacity, (2) convert to Dedicated pool, (3) expand host API usage — we’ll prepare a cost/benefit snapshot on request.

6) Suggested next steps (owner + timeline)
- Schedule review meeting — owner: CSM ({{CSM_NAME}}) — target: within 2 weeks
- Prepare renewal option summary — owner: AE / finance — target: 5 business days

Sign-off
Thanks,
{{CSM_NAME}}
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Tone variants (short / executive friendly)
- Short subject: "Quarterly recap: {{CUSTOMER_NAME}} + Redwood"
- Short body: "Hi {{SPONSOR_NAME}}, quick recap: uptime {{UPTIME}}, p95 {{P95_LATENCY}}, tokens +{{%}}. Recommend 30m to align on renewal/options — when’s good? — {{CSM_NAME}}"

3) Renewal playbook (lightweight step-by-step)
Trigger: contract approaching 90–120 days before expiry OR usage spike indicating likely expansion.
Risk signals (score 0–5):
- Usage trend flat/decreasing (3)
- Exec sponsor inactive > 90 days (4)
- Major incident in last 60 days (4)
- Contract under-budgeted for growth (3)
- Procurement freeze or legal delay (5)

Action sequence (owner tags)
- 90d: Internal health review + create renewal brief (CSM)
- 75d: Send executive recap email + request 20–30m sponsor touchpoint (CSM + AE cc)
- 60d: Present renewal options + price anchor (AE + Finance)
- 45d: Negotiate terms; legal checklist (AE + Legal)
- 21d: Final confirmation + PO or E-sign (AE/CSM)
- <14d: Escalation to AM director and Solutions Eng for risk mitigation

Escalation path (contact order)
1) Account AE
2) CSM lead (Priya Raman)
3) Solutions Eng lead (Jordan Lee)
4) CS Director (Marta Alvarez)

4) Mini renewal tracker (paste into sheet / CRM)
Columns (recommended spreadsheet headers):
- Account, Sponsor, Renewal date, Contract value, Forecasted outcome (win/at-risk), Health score (0–10), Last sponsor touch (date), Next step (text), Owner, Notes.
Sample row to copy:
{{CUSTOMER_NAME}}, {{SPONSOR_NAME}}, 2025-07-31, $320,000, at-risk, 6, 2025-01-10, Schedule sponsor touch, Priya Raman, "Capacity forecast shows 15% shortfall"

5) Quick examples: objections and suggested language
- If sponsor says "We’re cutting budget": "Understood. Can we align on highest-impact usage we should preserve? We can model a reduced commitment that keeps critical routes in Dedicated while scaling non-critical traffic on hosted API."
- If technical risk: "We’ll commit a Solutions Eng session to validate performance and provide a remediation timeline; we can include acceptance criteria in the renewal appendix."

6) Pre-send QA checklist for the quarterly recap email
- Replace all placeholders (sponsor, KPIs, dates)
- Attach one-page snapshot PDF or include in-body bullets
- Confirm subject line matches recipient level (executive vs practitioner)
- CC relevant reps (AE, Solutions Eng, legal if pricing included)
- Set follow-up task in CRM with next-step date

Open items / TODOs for this template
- Decide standard health score formula to include in snapshot (action: agree on metrics with CS team) — owner: Priya Raman — due: 2025-02-05
- Determine whether to include unit economics (cost per 1k tokens) in executive emails by default — owner: AE team — due: 2025-02-12

References / links
- Confluence: account-playbooks (CONFLUENCE-12345)
- Jira: JIRA-CS-998 (renewal tracking board)

Notes to self
Keep iterations lightweight; this doc should be a copy/pasteable source for CSMs and AEs. Collect two live examples per quarter to convert into short case bullets in the recap email.
